source.title: Self-Ablating Transformers: More Interpretability, Less Sparsity
source.authors: J. Ferrao; Luhan Mikaelson; Keenan Pepper; Natalia Pérez-Campanero Antolin

page_placements.theme: Architecture, training and regularization shape specialization

record.tranche_reason: The study trains small GPT-Neo models with self-ablation and measures SAE feature sparsity and reconstruction, a different-method test of the SAE-recoverability part of V4. It does not test the original toy-model superposition setup.
record.gate_note: The tested models are trained with an intentional self-ablation constraint; their results are not evidence that the same specialization arises spontaneously. The study does not measure superposition geometry, feature overlap, feature importance, polysemanticity caused by capacity pressure, canonical SAE units, or feature dimensionality. Table 1's SAE L0 and CE results are included for V4. Its L1-norm results are included as related findings under fits_no_version. Other interpretability metrics do not directly measure a claim version.
record.test_reason: SAEs serve only as an interpretability yardstick to compare self-ablated models, trained with a deliberate kWTA constraint, against a baseline. The study never asks whether the model's features are superposed or SAE-recoverable. It reports only the SAE L0 and CE gains of its own method. The single baseline SAE (L0 7.22, CE 0.63 on a 3M TinyStories model) is a setup value, not a test of V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors conclude self-ablation improves interpretability on ACDC, SAE, neuron-explanation and N2G measures, with at most a 20% perplexity increase. They say it reduces overall sparsity (higher L1), so the gains come from specialization and localization rather than sparsity. They caution that TinyStories and small scale limit generalization. Note that the intro calls the L1 an activation norm, while Section 4.5 defines it on weights.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses jointly trained GPT-Neo models with learned k-winner-takes-all gating and evaluates SAE reconstruction; it does not reproduce the original toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: SAE L0 and CE values vary with ablation type (global or local) and k.

fits_no_version.finding: kWTA self-ablation training lowers SAE L0 (7.22 to 4.01–5.48) and raises the CE score (0.63 to 0.65–0.72) versus the baseline. It also raises normalized weight L1 (0.44 to 0.62–0.76).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-time kWTA gating yields activations that an SAE reconstructs with fewer active features, without lowering weight L1.

fits_no_version.finding: The self-ablated global k=2 model has a higher mean neuron explanation score (0.46 vs 0.41). Its N2G graph density is lower, and its neuron entropy and token diversity are lower in later layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-time kWTA gating increases neuron specialization and monosemanticity proxies in small transformers.

record.problems: The experiments use relatively small models and the linguistically simple TinyStories dataset. The authors state that scaling to larger architectures is unknown. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the listed SAE metrics.
record.rows_left_out: Other Table 1 outcomes, Table 2 layerwise graph metrics, and neuron-explanation scores are omitted because they do not directly test a claim version or the SAE-recoverability measurement recorded here.

untested.parts: No toy model and no study of geometry or the sparsity transition.
No test of capacity competition or of dedicated versus shared dimensions.
No test of polysemanticity arising without capacity pressure.
SAEs are used only as a metric. There is no test of whether features are distributed or SAE-recoverable in LLMs.
No test of the completeness, stability or canonicity of SAE features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' and its V4 labels are not justified. SAE metrics here benchmark the authors' intervention, which is induced on purpose, and the paper makes no claim about superposition or SAE recoverability. No uncertainty is reported, and there is only one SAE per model at a single layer (blocks.6.hook_mlp_out).

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, overlapping nearly orthogonal directions, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether polysemanticity results from feature competition for limited capacity, or important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure.
The models are small GPT-Neo models trained on TinyStories, not tests across large language models; the study does not test features spread across many neurons.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional.

relation.reason: The study uses SAE feature decomposition as an evaluation tool for self-ablation, without testing overlapping feature geometry, capacity explanations, dictionary completeness or feature dimensionality.

tranche.reason: SAEs evaluate the interpretability and reconstruction performance of deliberately induced self-ablation representations. The reported comparisons assess the study's method rather than independently testing a superposition claim version.

source_check.notes: The authors' at-most-20% perplexity assertion conflicts with Table 1's increase from 5.73 to 6.97. Section 4.5 defines L1 using model weights; the introduction inconsistently calls it an activation norm.
